results.notes: Degree, indexed-neighbor and pair queries. Global upper bound over all maximum degrees. Uses neighbor greedy below √n and a pair-query routine above √n. The plot shows the leading n-power only; polylogarithmic factors remain in the bound label.

results.guarantee: cΔ colors, for every fixed c>1; hence Δ+1; An explicit proper color for every vertex
results.notes: Indexed-neighbor and pair queries, even with all degrees supplied. A global worst-case lower bound. The displayed construction has N=2s vertices and Δ=√s+1, so Δ=Θ(√N). It does not establish Ω(n^{3/2}) at every fixed Δ. The output may use cΔ colors, which includes Δ+1 for sufficiently large degree.

results.guarantee: Δ+1 colors; An explicit proper color for every vertex
results.notes: Neighbor and pair queries, with degree queries to determine Δ. Selects the cheaper of O(nΔ) greedy and O(n² log n/Δ) pair queries. For Δ≥1 this gives O(n + min{nΔ,n² log n/Δ}); the largest envelope is O(n^{3/2}√log n), near Δ=√(n log n). Correctness is Las Vegas: a color is accepted only after its color class has been checked.

upsertSlices.task: Explicit proper coloring under distinct degeneracy palette contracts
assumptions: κ denotes graph degeneracy, not maximum degree.
Theorems 22–23 give the same query order with κ unknown or supplied.
A fixed additive λ and a sublinear relative slack o(κ) are distinct requirements.
Classical randomized algorithm; known vertex set [n].
Query budget can be enforced by aborting exceptional runs.

results.guarantee: κ+λ colors; integer λ>1; An explicit proper color for every vertex
results.notes: Pair and indexed-neighbor queries; lower holds also when κ is given. For each admissible hard family, additive slack λ yields the stated query lower bound. The overview specializes to a fixed integer λ>1, so its marker is at n². This does not match the different κ+o(κ) palette contract of the upper bound.

results.guarantee: κ+o(κ), with κ+1 for the sparse branch; An explicit proper color for every vertex
results.notes: Pair and indexed-neighbor queries with ⊥ end markers. No prior κ is needed. The algorithm first scans the graph; if κ≤√n it obtains a κ+1 coloring. Otherwise it uses a random partition, giving (1+O(1/log n))κ colors. Thus κ+o(κ) is an asymptotic shorthand, not a promise of κ colors at fixed small κ.

results.sourceLocation: Abstract and §1.1 consequence; §8 Theorem 4 and “Query model” paragraphs
results.notes: §8 explicitly enumerates indexed-neighbor and indexed-palette queries, both allowing ⊥. The advertised Õ(n√n) runtime implies no more primitive queries in its stated unit-cost model. §8 inherits construction steps from ACK19/AA20 while enumerating neighbor and palette operations; the precise inherited pair-access convention is not explicit in those paragraphs. Retained separately as a source-reported list-input result, without a normalized ordinary-combined-oracle point.

results.bound: O(n) expected bits; O(n) expected rounds
results.guarantee: Δ+1 colors; Both parties learn the full same coloring
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1, §3; round comparison confirmed in CMNS25 §1.1
results.notes: Two parties hold disjoint portions of the edge set; n and Δ supplied. This is a communication budget, not a graph-query count. The original record omitted the expectation qualifier for bits. Theorem 1 is zero error; Corollary 1.1 instead gives a constant-error private-coin worst-case-bit variant, not used as the plotted protocol.

results.guarantee: Δ+1 colors; hard graphs have Δ=2; Bob (and hence both parties) learns a proper full coloring
results.notes: Two-party edge partition; lower already holds with all edges at Alice. The proof encodes independent bits in degree-two gadgets. It lower-bounds the global worst-case communication budget, and supplies no interaction-round lower bound. Zero-error expected-bit optimality follows by truncation and Markov’s inequality (an explicit atlas inference).

results.bound: O(n) expected bits; O(loglog n · log Δ) worst-case rounds
results.guarantee: Δ+1 colors; Both parties learn the full same coloring
results.notes: Two parties hold a disjoint edge partition; n and Δ supplied. The rare unsuccessful sparsification triggers transmission of the full graph, so the output remains correct. This fallback preserves the worst-case round bound while the communication bound remains expected. Logs are conventionally truncated below a constant for small n and Δ.
